target.title: fix: tighten control ui input validation [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where edge-case Control UI preview inputs and assistant media filenames were accepted more broadly than needed, which could produce unnecessary upstream requests or less predictable download headers.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change tightens shared object-key filtering, validates GitHub preview repository names before any preview fetch, normalizes GitHub avatar URLs to a small deterministic request shape, and sanitizes assistant media filenames before building response headers. The patch keeps the existing Control UI and config merge behavior for valid inputs.

## User Impact

Users should see the same behavior for normal GitHub issue and pull request previews and normal assistant media downloads. Invalid preview targets, unsafe avatar URLs, and unusual media filenames are now handled more conservatively.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change.

- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/prototype-keys.test.ts src/config/merge-patch.proto-pollution.test.ts src/gateway/control-ui-github-preview.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts -t 'sanitizes control characters|caps long'`

Remote validation was not available in this environment: Blacksmith Testbox was missing its CLI and direct AWS Crabbox required broker login.

target.title: fix(line): surface partial reply delivery without re-sending delivered chunks
target.body:
Fixes #106333

## What Problem This Solves

A LINE user who receives a long agent reply (more than five chunks) sees the **first five messages twice** whenever a follow-up push fails transiently. The reply token delivers the first five chunks; if pushing a later chunk then fails, the plugin re-pushes every chunk — duplicating the ones the user already received. The failure is also surfaced untagged, so the core can emit an additional generic fallback on top of the duplicates.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `sendLineReplyChunks`, one `try` wrapped the reply send, the remaining-push loop, and the `return`, so a push failure *after* a successful reply was caught by the same `catch` that handles a genuine reply-token failure and fell through to the "push everything" fallback.

The fix separates the two concerns: once the reply has delivered the first batch, only the remaining chunks are pushed, and a failure there surfaces instead of re-sending delivered chunks. Any error propagated after content already reached the user is tagged so `isVisiblePartialDeliveryError` (`src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) recognises it and the core suppresses a duplicate fallback — the same contract the rich/media partial path already uses. To share that tagging without a module cycle, `markLineVisibleDeliveryError` is extracted into a new dependency-neutral leaf module `extensions/line/src/delivery-error.ts`, imported by both `reply-chunks.ts` and `auto-reply-delivery.ts` (no `reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery` cycle). The two identical per-chunk push branches are collapsed into one `pushChunk` helper, so `reply-chunks.ts` is net shorter.

Independent of the open reliability PRs in this area (e.g. #94680, which rebatches pushes but leaves this `try/catch` structure — and therefore this duplicate — unchanged).

## User Impact

Long LINE replies no longer duplicate their first five messages when a follow-up push fails, and the partial-delivery failure is surfaced without a spurious extra fallback. No behavior change for replies that fit the reply token or that succeed.

## Evidence

### Red / green regression test

New test in `reply-chunks.test.ts`: the reply delivers `one`..`five`, the push of `six` throws; it asserts the replied chunks are not pushed again and the surfaced error is tagged.

On current `main` (bug present):

```
 × does not re-send reply-delivered chunks when a later push fails
AssertionError: expected [ 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', …(1) ] to not include 'one'
 ❯ extensions/line/src/reply-chunks.test.ts:215:24
    215|     expect(pushed).not.toContain("one");
 Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

With this change:

```
 Tests  5 passed (5)
```
### Real LINE chat — before vs after (live account)

Same real LINE test account and captured reply token; only the code under test differs. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch, chunk 6 is 5001 chars so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine HTTP 400.

**Before (current `main`) — `c1`..`c5` delivered twice (duplicate):**

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-before.png)

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change) — `c1`..`c5` delivered once:**

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-after.png)

```
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

### End-to-end (real delivery path)

Driving the real `deliverLineAutoReply` → real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the same scenario:

- on `main`: `one`..`five` are re-pushed (duplicates);
- with this change: only the chunk after the failure is pushed, `one`..`five` are never re-pushed, and the thrown error carries `{ sentBeforeError: true, visibleReplySent: true }`.

### Real LINE run (live account + API)

Captured a real reply token from an inbound webhook, then drove the real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the real LINE reply/push API. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch; chunk 6 is 5001 characters, so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine **HTTP 400** (recipient/token redacted):

**Before (current `main`)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the fallback re-pushes every chunk, so `c1`..`c5` are delivered **twice**:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the delivered chunks are **not** re-sent; the error is tagged:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

In the LINE chat, `c1`..`c5` appear twice before the fix and exactly once after.

### Checks

```
oxfmt --check              → clean (4 files)
oxlint                     → 0 problems
tsgo (extensions)          → no errors in the touched files
check:import-cycles        → 0 runtime value cycles
check:madge-import-cycles  → 0 cycles (reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery cycle removed)
LINE suite                 → reply-chunks.test.ts + auto-reply-delivery.test.ts: 14 passed
```
